title: From 3D model to posted video
lede: Your first video, start to finish: the arena that sits on a train station. One small step at a time. Do the step, tap the green button, move on.

steps.title: Part 1 of 9 · Pick one name for all three apps
do: Think of a short name about places and their stories.
Check it is free on [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com) and [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com).
Use the exact same @name on all three.
steps.see: The same @name is free on all three apps.
steps.tip: Leave the word stadium out of the name. You will grow past stadiums.

steps.title: Set up TikTok
steps.where: TikTok app on your phone, then **Profile** at the bottom right.
do: Sign up with your email.
Add the name, a profile photo and a one-line bio.
Keep it a personal account for now.
steps.see: Your profile page with the new name.
steps.tip: Business accounts lose most popular songs. Stay personal until you have a reason to switch.

steps.title: Set up Instagram as a creator
steps.where: Instagram app, **Profile**, then the three lines at the top right.
do: Tap **Account type and tools**.
Tap **Switch to professional account**.
Choose **Creator**.
steps.see: A **Professional dashboard** button on your profile.
steps.tip: A creator account gives you free view stats and scheduling.

steps.title: Set up a YouTube channel
do: Sign in with your Google account.
Click **Create channel**.
Use the same name and photo as the other apps.
steps.see: An empty channel dashboard.
steps.tip: YouTube Shorts keep getting found through search for months. TikTok mostly does not.

steps.title: Get the free tools
do: Install [CapCut](https://www.capcut.com) for the desktop. This is your video editor.
Bookmark [Adobe Podcast Enhance](https://podcast.adobe.com/enhance). It cleans up your voice.
Bookmark the [YouTube Audio Library](https://studio.youtube.com) (left menu, **Audio library**). Free music.
Install [Blender](https://www.blender.org/download/) now so it is ready later.
steps.see: CapCut opens to its home screen.
steps.tip: Backup editor if CapCut is not available: [DaVinci Resolve](https://www.blackmagicdesign.com/products/davinciresolve), free and more powerful.

steps.title: Find your video folder
do: Open **01-msg-penn-station**. Claude made it for you.
Inside: **script.md**, plus **clips**, **voice** and **export** folders.
**_template** is the blank copy for every future video.
steps.see: Four items in the first video folder.
steps.tip: Same folders every time is how a template keeps you fast and uniform.

steps.title: Part 2 of 9 · Read up on the story
steps.where: Your browser, plus **script.md** open in TextEdit.
do: Read [the old Penn Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania_Station_%281910%E2%80%931963%29) page.
Read the [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden) page.
Write 3 facts that surprised you under **Sources**, each with its link.
steps.see: Three facts with links in script.md.
steps.tip: Check every number in a second place, like the [NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission](https://www.nyc.gov/site/lpc/about/about-lpc.page) site or a news story.

steps.title: Part 3 of 9 · Write the hook
do: Read the three sample hooks.
Write one of your own.
Keep the one that makes you think: wait, what?
steps.see: One hook line you would stop scrolling for.
steps.tip: The first 2 seconds decide if anyone watches. Lead with the strangest true fact.

steps.title: Rewrite the script in your own words
do: Follow the shape: hook, setup, twist, payoff, question.
Change any line that does not sound like you.
Read it out loud with a timer. Aim for 45 to 60 seconds.
steps.see: A script that sounds like you talking to a friend.
steps.tip: About 140 spoken words fill 60 seconds. Shorter usually wins.

steps.title: Fact check every line
do: Match each date and number to a source.
Say opinions as questions, like the last line does.
Cut anything you cannot back up.
steps.see: Every fact in the script has a source.
steps.tip: History comments are brutal about mistakes. One wrong date can take over the comments.

steps.title: Check the shot list
do: Read each row: which line, which style, which camera move, which on-screen text.
Change any shot you want.
Aim for a new shot every 2 to 3 seconds.
steps.see: A shot for every line of the script.
steps.tip: Pick 2 or 3 styles you use in every video. That repeated look is your brand.

steps.title: Find old photos you are allowed to use
do: Search "Pennsylvania Station New York".
Only pick photos marked **No known restrictions** or **Public domain**.
Save them to the **clips** folder.
Copy the credit line into **Photo credits** in script.md.
steps.see: Two or three old photos with credits written down.
steps.tip: A random photo from Google Images can get your video taken down. Stick to these two sites.

steps.title: Part 4 of 9 · Drop in photos of the real building
do: Screenshot the top-down view in [Google Maps](https://www.google.com/maps) satellite mode.
Add aerial shots from each side, the entrance and the inside bowl.
Name them like **top-down.jpg** or **aerial-north.jpg**.
Fill in **notes.md**. Short answers are fine.
steps.see: Five or more photos and a filled-in notes.md.
steps.tip: The README in the references folder lists the best photos to grab, in order.

steps.title: Ask Claude to rebuild the model
do: Type: Rebuild Madison Square Garden using the photos in references.
Compare the new model to your photos.
Name the 3 things that still look wrong. Claude fixes them.
steps.see: A model you would recognize from the street.
steps.tip: Specific notes beat general ones. "The drum is too short" helps more than "looks off".

steps.title: Part 5 of 9 · Set up the screen to record
do: Make Chrome full screen with [[Cmd + Ctrl + F]].
Click **Madison Square Garden** at the top.
Make sure **Showcase** is selected.
Turn on Do Not Disturb so no pop-ups land in your shot.
steps.see: The arena filling most of the screen.
steps.tip: In Showcase, each style click glides the camera to a new angle. Those glides are your camera moves.

steps.title: Record one shot
do: Press [[Cmd + Shift + 5]].
Click **Record Selected Portion** in the toolbar.
Drag a tall box over the arena, shaped like a phone. Keep the side panel out.
Click **Record**, then click a style and wait for the camera to stop.
Press [[Cmd + Ctrl + Esc]] to stop.
steps.see: A new video file on your Desktop.
steps.tip: In the toolbar, **Options**, then **Save to**, lets you pick the clips folder instead.

steps.title: Record every shot on the list
steps.where: Same setup as the last step.
do: Record each row of the shot list as its own file.
Record each one twice. Keep the smoother one.
Rename them to match the list, like **03-cutaway.mov**.
For a slow orbit, click **Explore** and drag slowly while recording.
steps.see: One clip per shot in the **clips** folder.
steps.tip: Ask Claude for a record button that saves clean vertical clips straight from the page. It skips the cropping.

steps.title: Blender, the other 3D option
steps.where: Read this step. Nothing to click yet.
do: Our code engine: fast, same look every time, and it can power the map site later.
[Blender](https://www.blender.org): film-quality light, smooth camera paths, but slow to learn.
Best of both: Claude can add an export button so our models open in Blender.
City around the arena: the [Blosm add-on](https://prochitecture.gumroad.com/l/blender-osm) brings in real buildings from [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org).
steps.see: You know when to use which.
steps.tip: Start videos with the code engine. Learn Blender on the side for the shots that need more polish.

steps.title: Learn Blender basics, on the side
steps.where: [Blender Guru on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@blenderguru), the beginner donut series.
do: Watch one part per sitting. Follow along in Blender.
Stop after the parts on materials, camera and rendering.
You do not need the whole series.
steps.see: You can move around a scene, light it and render one picture.
steps.tip: Credit [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright) in your caption whenever you use its map data.

steps.title: Set Blender to vertical video
steps.where: Blender, the **Properties** panel on the right, the printer icon (**Output**).
do: Set **Resolution X** to 1080.
Set **Resolution Y** to 1920.
Set **Frame Rate** to 30.
steps.see: The camera view turns into a tall phone shape.
steps.tip: Save this as your start file: **File**, **Defaults**, **Save Startup File**.

steps.title: Part 6 of 9 · Record your voice
steps.where: A quiet room. A closet full of clothes works great.
do: Plug in your mic. Keep it about a hand's width from your mouth.
Open QuickTime Player, then **File**, **New Audio Recording**.
Read the script three times in a row. Smile while you read.
Save to the **voice** folder.
steps.see: One audio file with three full takes.
steps.tip: Later, for an AI voice, [ElevenLabs](https://elevenlabs.io) is the common pick (paid plans start around $5 a month). Label it when you post.

steps.title: Clean up the audio
do: Upload your voice file.
Lower the strength slider to about 70 percent if it sounds robotic.
Download the cleaned file to the **voice** folder.
steps.see: Your voice sounds clear with no room echo.
steps.tip: Claude can also clean it for you with the Adobe Enhance Speech connection.

steps.title: Part 7 of 9 · Start a vertical project
do: Click **Create project**.
Import your clips, old photos and the cleaned voice.
Drag the voice onto the timeline first.
Set the ratio above the preview to **9:16**.
steps.see: A tall, phone-shaped preview with your voice on the timeline.
steps.tip: Voice first, pictures second. The words set the rhythm.

steps.title: Lay the shots over the voice
do: Put each shot above the line it matches.
Split clips with [[Cmd + B]] and delete the extra.
Change the shot every 2 to 3 seconds.
Give old photos a slow zoom so they feel alive.
steps.see: Pictures that change in time with your words.
steps.tip: Your strongest shot goes first, with the hook written on it.

steps.title: Add captions
steps.where: CapCut, the **Captions** or **Text** tab, then **Auto captions**.
do: Let CapCut write the captions from your voice.
Fix every wrong word, especially names.
Move them to the middle of the screen.
steps.see: Easy-to-read words that match your voice.
steps.tip: Most people watch with the sound off. Captions are not optional.

steps.title: Add music and sound
do: Download one track from the [YouTube Audio Library](https://studio.youtube.com) or [Pixabay Music](https://pixabay.com/music/).
Drop it under the voice and turn it way down.
Add a whoosh on the cutaway reveal.
steps.see: Music you can feel but your voice stays clear.
steps.tip: Popular songs can get your video muted. Trending sounds are safest added inside each app.

steps.title: Check it on your phone
steps.where: Export a test copy, AirDrop it to your phone, play it full screen.
do: Can you read every word?
Is anything hidden behind the right-side buttons or the bottom caption area?
Does the first second make you want to keep watching?
steps.see: Clean text, nothing covered, a strong opening.
steps.tip: Keep words out of the bottom fifth and the right edge. The apps put buttons there.

steps.title: Export the final video
do: Save it to the **export** folder.
If a CapCut ending clip appears, delete it and export again.
steps.see: One finished MP4 in the export folder.
steps.tip: Upload this same clean file to every app. Never repost one app's download to another.

steps.title: Part 8 of 9 · Write the post text
do: One line that adds to the hook, then your question.
Add 3 to 5 hashtags, like #nyc #history #architecture.
Add the photo credits from script.md.
steps.see: A caption ready to paste three times.
steps.tip: Pick a cover frame now too: the most striking shot, with short title text.

steps.title: Post to TikTok
do: Upload the MP4 and paste the caption.
Choose your cover frame.
Post now, or click **Schedule** for a set time.
steps.see: The video is live or scheduled.
steps.tip: With an AI voice, turn on the [AI-generated content label](https://support.tiktok.com/en/using-tiktok/creating-videos/ai-generated-content).

steps.title: Post to Instagram Reels
steps.where: Instagram app, or [Meta Business Suite](https://business.facebook.com) on your Mac to schedule.
do: Create a new **Reel** and upload the MP4.
Paste the caption and pick the cover.
Share it, or schedule it.
steps.see: The Reel on your profile.
steps.tip: Posting at a different hour than TikTok is fine. Same day is good.

steps.title: Post to YouTube Shorts
do: Upload the MP4. Vertical and under 3 minutes makes it a Short.
Title it like a search: Why Madison Square Garden Sits on Penn Station.
Choose **No, it's not made for kids**, then publish or schedule.
steps.see: The video listed under **Shorts** in your channel.
steps.tip: For an AI voice, read YouTube's [altered content rules](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/14328491).

steps.title: Reply to comments in the first hour
steps.where: All three apps, on your phone.
do: Reply to every real comment.
Pin the best one to the top.
Ignore trolls. If someone shows a real mistake, thank them and pin the correction.
steps.see: Conversations under your video.
steps.tip: Replies tell the app people care, which shows your video to more people.

steps.title: Part 9 of 9 · Find where people left
steps.where: Two days later: TikTok **Analytics**, Instagram **View insights**, YouTube Studio **Analytics**.
do: Find the retention chart on each video.
Note the second where the line drops the most.
Write it, and your guess why, under **After posting** in script.md.
steps.see: One clear thing to fix next time.
steps.tip: That drop-off second is your best teacher. Fix one thing per video.

steps.title: Batch the next four videos
do: Copy **_template** four times and name each next stadium.
Write all four scripts in one sitting.
Then record all the shots, then edit all four.
Aim for 2 or 3 posts a week.
steps.see: A week of videos ready before the week starts.
steps.tip: Ask Claude to build the next stadiums from your reference photos while you write.

steps.title: Point your bio at a home base
do: For now, link your YouTube channel, or a free [Linktree](https://linktr.ee) page.
Later, swap in your map site: explore every stadium from the videos.
steps.see: A link in all three bios.
steps.tip: Social media brings people in. Your own site is the part nobody can take away.

stuck.problem: The recording captured the whole screen.
stuck.fix: Press [[Cmd + Shift + 5]] again and click **Record Selected Portion** before **Record**.
Close other apps and tabs, plug in the charger, and draw a smaller box.

stuck.problem: The 3D model does not look like the real building.
stuck.fix: Add more top-down and aerial photos to the references folder, then tell Claude the 3 biggest differences.

stuck.problem: CapCut asks you to pay for Pro.
stuck.fix: Pro is about $10 a month. Try the free [DaVinci Resolve](https://www.blackmagicdesign.com/products/davinciresolve) first, or ask Claude which feature you really need.

stuck.problem: My video got muted or flagged for music.
stuck.fix: Swap the track for one from the [YouTube Audio Library](https://studio.youtube.com) and upload again.

stuck.problem: Captions are cut off on the phone.
stuck.fix: Move them up toward the middle and make the text box narrower.

stuck.problem: Barely any views after the first few videos.
stuck.fix: That is normal for the first 2 to 6 months. Check the drop-off second, sharpen the hook, keep posting.

stuck.problem: People are arguing in the comments.
stuck.fix: Check your source. If you were wrong, pin a correction. If not, let it go. Never argue.

finish_title: Your first video is out there.
finish_text: That is the hardest one. Every video after this uses the same folders, the same looks and the same steps, and gets faster. Take a break, then pick the next four stadiums.
footer: From 3D model to posted video, version 1. November 2026.
